editorial.headline: Recreational Equipment Rental: Open Nationally, Closed to PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: A broad rental activity for leisure and sports equipment, open to foreign investment nationally but blocked for PMA registration throughout Bali.
editorial.body:
A foreign-owned company cannot register this activity in Bali today. The provincial position is not limited to one type of equipment: every scope in this activity is assessed in OSS at the Besar scale as Low or Medium-Low risk, placing it within Bali’s island-wide, permanent moratorium on PMA for those risk classes. The record identifies the block with the Bali moratorium of 13 May 2026. That result sits alongside the national position: nationally, the activity is open to PMA, with foreign ownership permitted up to 100%.

Nationally, this is an activity for renting and operational leasing recreation and sports equipment without an option to buy. Its practical range is deliberately broad: recreational boats, canoes, sailboats and yachts supplied without an operator; bicycles, including electric bicycles; beach chairs and umbrellas; and other sporting equipment, including ski equipment. The boundaries are equally important. It does not cover boat hire with crew, water transport equipment hired for passengers or goods, media and other personal or household goods, or equipment rental that is an integrated part of a recreational facility.

The activity is open at Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scales. That wide national scale availability should not be read as a Bali PMA pathway. In Bali, the large-scale OSS risk assessment applies across every scope of this activity, and the provincial moratorium blocks PMA registration for Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI on an island-wide, permanent basis. The restriction therefore reaches the activity as a whole rather than only a particular item of equipment.

For founders, the distinction is straightforward but consequential: the national foreign-ownership ceiling describes what is permitted nationally, while Bali’s moratorium determines whether PMA registration can proceed there. A national 100% foreign-ownership ceiling does not make PMA registration available in Bali. This activity remains nationally open, but Bali is not presently a place where a foreign-owned company can register it.
